notes: Clean Token methods (`isBlockOpen`/`isBlockClose`) are applied consistently, including the import mapping key, plus a good end-to-end adapt test; it misses the quoted-address HasSuffix check and leaves the quoted "{}" branch as before.

Clean Token helper methods mirror the reference and are applied consistently (including the anonymous-block check); it only misses the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` tweak, and it adds good parser tests plus an end-to-end adapt test.

Fixes every structural brace check that the reference touches, including address-suffix handling and the quoted "{}" fall-through, except the import mapping-key check; the repeated inline `Val()=="{" && !Quoted()` checks are less clean than a helper, but the tests are thorough.

Correctly adds unquoted-brace checks across the dispenser and parser and matches the reference's `{}` handling, but repeats the `Val()==X && !Quoted()` check inline everywhere instead of using a helper, and misses the anonymous-block check in doImport; tests are thorough at both the dispenser and parser level.

The core fix with dispenser helpers is complete and clean, but it adds an unrequested feature that carries quotedness through import args, using duplicated placeholder regex parsing; in the variadic loop the reused token leaks quotedness onto later unquoted args.

The core fix with helper methods is sound and complete, but it also carries quotedness of import arguments into snippet placeholders, which reimplements placeholder parsing in `quotedImportArg` and changes token-quoting semantics beyond what the issue asked for.

Fixes the reported for_each case, but it drops module instance keys when deduplicating, so a root import for `module.child[0]` suppresses the child block for every instance; it also adds no expansion-time dedup, so dynamic parent targets lose to child targets, and it makes unneeded changes to the configs package and transform_config.

Fixes the reported static for_each case, but parent-over-child precedence is broken in two ways, and one hidden test fails. It never adds a dedup check at expansion time, so dynamic child imports overwrite parent ones. It also discards module keys during static dedup, so a child import is dropped for every module instance. On top of that it makes unrelated edits to configs and transform_config.

Returns a slice and dedups static targets on the full instance address, then adds the same expansion-time parent-first dedup as the reference, and covers for_each, count, mixed and expanded-module precedence cases with thorough tests.

Matches the reference approach: it returns a list of statements and dedups with knownImports at expansion, so parent precedence is correct. It also adds a static instance-level dedup that is redundant but harmless. Tests are thorough, covering for_each, count, mixed static/dynamic imports and precedence with an expanded module.

Matches the reference approach with an extra keyed static-instance dedup and an unrequested first-wins change for unknownImports; tests are good but include a redundant hand-rolled loop and a weak unit test that compares Range strings.

Correct overall: it dedups at expansion like the reference and adds a static instance-level dedup. However, the O(n²) loop recomputes static addresses on every pass, and it makes an unrequested first-wins change to unknownImports. Tests cover the main scenarios, but the refactoring unit test is weak and may rely on an unexported helper from an external test package.
